opening_message:
Ticket 1: Miguel Benson (employee ID E006) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E006.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Miguel Benson (E006) is a full-time Engineer and requests admin access to Source Code. Since Engineers own the Source Code system, admin is permitted for full-time employees under policy. Recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E006 (Miguel Benson) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Under policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds the maximum; recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR's database lists Miguel Benson (E006) as full-time, but Security's database (looked up before writing) lists him as a contractor with basic security training. Under the access policy, a contractor with basic training may have at most read access and never admin, while a full-time Engineer who owns Source Code could have admin. Given the conflicting records and that Security's lookup specifically identifies contractor status with basic training, the maximum allowable level is read. The requested admin exceeds this maximum, so I grant read.
